units.function: Behavioral shell tests for Docker entrypoint UID/GID remapping, application-home ownership repair, privilege drop and arbitrary non-root execution.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> sh scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh -> PATH-stubbed Linux commands and a temporary filesystem; no real container runtime, user namespace, volume driver, Kubernetes policy or server readiness.
units.keyDataModels: Current/requested UID/GID, node user/group, PAPERCLIP_HOME ownership mismatch, root versus arbitrary non-root process and forwarded command argv.
units.lifecycle: Container starts -> root may remap node identity and repair home ownership -> gosu drops privileges and execs command; non-root process skips mutation, warns on mismatch and execs directly.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 9/9. The branching tests cover important Compose/OpenShift/Kubernetes shapes and ownership regressions, but all system commands are stubs. Target validation, invalid IDs, real filesystem semantics, failures, scale and readiness are untested.
units.designRationale: Ship one image that works with host-mapped Compose volumes and restricted arbitrary-UID platforms while avoiding costly chown on already-correct trees.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS self-hosted/local enterprise profile needs rootless-first deployment, predictable volume ownership and safe migration across Docker, Kubernetes and OpenShift without risking customer data paths.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the dual root/rootless test matrix, privilege drop, explicit command exec and conditional ownership repair. Make rootless the preferred profile; resolve and validate an allowlisted dedicated data root, reject broad/symlink targets, validate UID/GID and collisions, verify writability/readiness, bound or document recursive repair and test actual container images in CI.
units.responsibilityConflict: This is deployment mechanics rather than work responsibility, but root-time ownership mutation is a high-impact administrative action with no dry-run, target digest, operator evidence or rollback record.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL destructive-target gap: PAPERCLIP_HOME becomes a recursive root chown target with no tested rejection of /, empty, symlinked or unexpectedly broad paths. HIGH identity-remap gap: invalid/zero/negative/overflow UID/GID, existing-account collisions and usermod/groupmod/chown failures are untested. MEDIUM availability risk: recursive find/chown has no bound/progress/partial recovery and can delay large enterprise volumes. MEDIUM readiness gap: arbitrary non-root mismatch only warns and starts without proving data/config/log directories are writable.
